title: Pe Hebrew Letter (פ): Pe, Fe & Final Pe
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Pe (פ), also spelled Pey: its [p] sound with a dagesh, its [f] sound (Fe), final Pe (ף), words like פֶּה (mouth) and practice.

blocks.text: Pe Hebrew Letter (פ): Pe, Fe, Final Pe & Practice

Pey (פ) is the seventeenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In text with vowel points, פּ with a dagesh (the dot inside) is pronounced [p], like 'p' in 'pot'; פ without a dagesh is pronounced [f], like 'f' in 'fun'. Pey is one of five Hebrew letters with a regular form (פ) and a final form (ף), called Fey Sofit.

The Hebrew word 'פֶּה' [pe] means 'mouth'. The pronunciation guides in this lesson are learning aids, not IPA. They use a roughly as in 'father', e as in 'bet', and y as in 'yes'. Keep the e in [pe] steady, without adding a y sound. Hyphens show syllable breaks.
One Letter, Two Sounds

In modern Hebrew, Bet, Kaf, and Pey each have two pronunciations distinguished by a dagesh in text with vowel points. For Pey, פּ represents [p] and פ represents [f]. These are two different consonant sounds; the dot does not mean that you should pronounce a doubled consonant.
Fey (פ), without a dagesh, is pronounced [f], like 'f' in 'fun'.

illustration.label: Fey (Pey without Dagesh)
illustration.equivalent: Pey without a dot (dagesh) in its center, pronounced [f]. This form is called Fey.

blocks.text: The Hebrew word 'שָׂפָה' [sa-fa] means 'language'. The first letter is Sin (שׂ), with a dot on the upper left, giving [s]. Its Kamatz Gadol gives [a], making [sa]. Pey (פ) without a dagesh gives [f], and its Kamatz Gadol gives [a], making [fa]. Hey (ה) at the end of the word is silent here. Say two syllables, sa-fa, with the stress on fa.
Pey (פּ), with a dagesh, is pronounced [p], like 'p' in 'pot'.

illustration.label: Pey with Dagesh
illustration.equivalent: Pey with a dot (dagesh) in its center, pronounced [p]. Without the dot, it is pronounced [f].

blocks.text: The Hebrew word 'פּוֹעַל' [po-al] means 'verb', a word for an action or state. Pey (פּ) has a dagesh and gives [p]. Holam Male (וֹ) supplies [o], without a separate v sound. Ayin (ע) has a Patah, giving [a]. In the common modern pronunciation used here, Ayin has no separate consonant sound; some speakers pronounce it as a throat consonant. Lamed (ל) gives [l]. Say two syllables, po-al, with the stress on po; keep o and a separate.

Ordinary Hebrew writing usually omits vowel points and the dagesh. In that writing, פ can stand for [p] or [f]: you learn the pronunciation with the word and use context to identify it. In the pointed examples in this lesson, the presence or absence of a dagesh shows which sound to use.
Fey Sofit (ף) is the final form of Pey. In the words in this lesson, it appears at the end and represents [f].

illustration.label: Fey Sofit
illustration.equivalent: Final Pey: Pey with its stroke extended below the line, written at the end of a word and pronounced [f].

blocks.text: Fey Sofit (ף) is the final form of Pey and represents [f], as in אַף [af], 'nose'. In the words in this lesson, the regular form פ appears at the beginning or in the middle, and the final form ף appears at the end. 'Sofit' means 'final'.
Words to Practice:
mouth

The Hebrew word 'פֶּה' [pe] means 'mouth'. It has two letters: Pey (פּ) and Hey (ה). The dagesh gives Pey its [p] sound, and the Segol (ֶ) beneath it gives [e]. Hey at the end of the word is silent here. Say pe as one syllable.
beautiful

The Hebrew word 'יָפָה' [ya-fa] means 'beautiful' in the feminine singular, used with a feminine singular noun or to describe a woman or girl. It has three letters: Yud (י), Pey (פ), and Hey (ה). Yud gives [y], as in 'yes', and its Kamatz Gadol gives [a], making [ya]. Pey has no dagesh, so it gives [f]; its Kamatz Gadol gives [a], making [fa]. Hey at the end of the word is silent here. Say two syllables, ya-fa, with the stress on fa.
nose
The Hebrew word 'אַף' [af] means 'nose'. It has two letters: Alef (א) and Fey Sofit (ף). The Patah (ַ) beneath Alef gives [a], and Fey Sofit gives [f]. Say af as one syllable.
Conclusions

Let’s review what we’ve covered. In text with vowel points, Pey with a dagesh (פּ) represents [p], and Fey without a dagesh (פ) represents [f]. The final form ף, called Fey Sofit, represents [f] at the end of a word. You’ve practised these sounds in several words. Now, take a quick test to check your understanding!

exercises.prompt: How is the letter Pey (פּ) pronounced?
exercises.explanation: Pey (פּ) with a dagesh is pronounced as [ p ].

exercises.prompt: In text with vowel points, Fey without a dagesh (פ) and Fey Sofit (ף) both represent [f].
exercises.explanation: Both represent [f]; ף is the final form. Pey with a dagesh (פּ) represents [p].

exercises.prompt: Match each letter form to its pronunciation in text with vowel points.
exercises.explanation: Pey with a dagesh (פּ) represents [p]. Fey without a dagesh (פ) and Fey Sofit (ף) represent [f].
'Sofit' means 'final' and is used for letters that change shape at the end of words.

exercises.prompt: The final form of Pey that represents [f] is called Fey Sofit (ף).
exercises.explanation: Fey Sofit (ף) represents [f] and is used at the end of words, as in אַף [af], 'nose'.

exercises.prompt: How is the letter Fey Sofit (ף) pronounced?
exercises.explanation: Fey Sofit (ף) is pronounced the same as Fey (פ) – as [ f ].

exercises.prompt: Match the words to their translations.
exercises.explanation: אַף means 'nose', פֶּה means 'mouth', and יָפָה means 'beautiful' in the feminine singular.

exercises.prompt: Pey with a dagesh (פּ) is pronounced as [ p ], like in 'pot'.
exercises.explanation: Pey (פּ) with a dagesh has a hard [ p ] sound.

exercises.prompt: What is the correct pronunciation of 'פֶּה'?
What vowel sound does the Kamatz Gadol beneath Pey (פָּ) represent?
exercises.explanation: Kamatz Gadol represents [a], roughly as in 'father'. With Pey (פּ), it makes [pa]; no special vowel length is required.

exercises.prompt: The letter Hey (ה) at the end of a word is usually silent.
exercises.explanation: In most cases, Hey (ה) at the end of a word is silent.
אַף is pronounced as [ af ] and means 'nose'.

exercises.prompt: Which option shows a letter with a Patah vowel sign?
exercises.explanation: Patah is a small horizontal line beneath a letter and represents [a]. In ordinary modern Hebrew, Patah and Kamatz Gadol both represent [a], without a required difference in length.

exercises.prompt: How do you translate the word (אַף) into English?
Match the English words to their Hebrew translations.
exercises.explanation: 'Nose' is אַף, 'mouth' is פֶּה, and 'beautiful' in the feminine singular is יָפָה.

exercises.prompt: In text with vowel points, Fey Sofit (ף) and Fey without a dagesh (פ) represent different sounds.
exercises.explanation: Both represent [f]. Adding a dagesh to the regular form gives פּ, pronounced [p].
